text: Question: The nurse has taught a client who has sustained a right tibial fracture and had an external fixation device applied 36 hours ago. Which of the following statements by the client would indicate a correct understanding of the teaching? Select all that apply.
A. “I will use chlorhexidine to clean around the pins.”
B. “I should limit my daily consumption of foods high in vitamin D.”
C. “I should expect to see some redness around the external pins.”
D. “I know that the metal rods help steady my leg fracture as it is healing.”
E. “I will notify my doctor if I experience increased pressure to the point of pain around my heel.”

Correct answers: A. “I will use chlorhexidine to clean around the pins.”; D. “I know that the metal rods help steady my leg fracture as it is healing.”; E. “I will notify my doctor if I experience increased pressure to the point of pain around my heel.”
notes: • Pin sites are cleaned with an antiseptic such as chlorhexidine, using aseptic technique.
• The metal frame holds the fracture steady while it heals.
• Increasing pressure and pain, for example around the heel, may signal compartment syndrome and must be reported.
• Vitamin D (and calcium) helps bone healing, so it should not be limited.
• Redness at the pin sites should be reported as a possible infection rather than accepted as normal.
(Answer key not on the slide; worked out with NCLEX reasoning, so check it against your class notes.) The pin-site redness item is the least certain part of this key.
